To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

pressure overload in the early neonatal rat heart induces a transient increase in the total PKCs and in the expression of all PKCs studied, which is associated with an increase in the cytoskeletal and nuclear PKCs.

the total PKC, PKCalpha, delta and epsilon are significantly upregulated at the third postoperative day in the left ventricular homogenate of neonatal rats subjected to pressure overload, and that this upregulation does not affect the distribution of these enzymes among the cellular fractions.

pressure overload imposed at d2 transiently increases the activity and abundance of protein kinase C isoforms alpha, epsilon and delta in the left ventricular homogenate of rat hearts, and that this upregulation of PKC is associated with the acceleration of cardiac growth and remodeling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of PKC isoform expression in the signal transductions of the cardiac growth and development.
the early response of PKC in neonatal rat heart to pressure overload.
the role of protein kinase C (PK C) isoforms in the signal transductions of cardiac growth and the development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PKC is upregulated in the neonatal heart subjected to pressure overload.
PKCalpha and PKCdelta are the most likely candidates for the role of the mediator of the hypertrophic response of the heart in the early postnatal period.
PKCalpha and PKCepsilon are involved in the early phase of pressure-induced cardiac growth, while PKCdelta is involved in the late phase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PKCalpha, delta and epsilon isoforms undergo transient upregulations in pressure-overloaded rat hearts at postnatal day 2.
the PKCdelta is the only isoform which is upregulated in the cytosol and downregulated in the membrane-enrichment fraction.
PKCalpha plays a significant role in cardiac growth in the neonatal rat heart.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the early postnatal heart responds to pressure overload by the transient upregulation of all PKC isoforms, which is associated with the accelerated growth of the left ventricle.
the PKC isoforms are not equally distributed in the different cellular compartments in the heart of the rat subjected to pressure overload.
PKCdelta may play an important role in the signal transmission from the cell membrane to the nucleus during the early stages of the cardiac growth response to pressure overload.
